gaps.sentence: He's got a ___ of stamps from every country he's visited.
gaps.explanation: Noun form: collection (a group of collected items).

gaps.sentence: He was ___ to resign after the scandal.
gaps.explanation: 'be forced to do' = be made to do unwillingly.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ dull a lecture that people walked out.
gaps.explanation: so + adjective (+a + noun) + that… — the alternative emphatic pattern.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ the impression that the interview was today.
gaps.explanation: 'Under the impression that …' = believing, perhaps wrongly.

gaps.sentence: I'd rather walk than ___ the bus.
gaps.explanation: 'would rather do A than do B' — both bare infinitives.

gaps.sentence: She's the most generous person I've ___ met.
gaps.explanation: 'the best… I've ever seen/met' — 'ever' with superlatives.

gaps.sentence: The findings will be published in ___ course.
gaps.hint: in ___ course = at the right time
gaps.explanation: 'In due course' = eventually, when the time is right.

gaps.sentence: The meeting was put ___ until Thursday.
